subject: Tactical renewal: usage audit + prefetching plan
messages:
From: Alicia Mendoza <alicia@patchworklabs.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@patchworklabs.com
Date: 2025-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Usage snapshot and renewal timing

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the Q1 onboarding help — things are going well. We ran a quick internal audit of token usage for the last six weeks and attached a CSV with per-endpoint spends. Two quick highlights:

- Monthly token consumption spiked 52% after we rolled the new summarization pipeline (peak at 18k req/day).
- Latency is within SLO for single-request paths, but batch inference for nightly jobs is sometimes timing out and re-issuing (adds costs).

Our renewal is up in late June and the finance team wants a short ROI recap + a practical plan to keep costs predictable while we scale. High-level asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a short recommendation that mixes short-term burst credits + a staged commit that gives us room for the next 3 months?
2) Any quick prefetch/prefix-caching suggestions to reduce duplicate token spend on similar queries?

I've attached the usage CSV. We can loop in ops if you want deeper telemetry.

Appreciate any quick guidance — the renewal owner wants to get a follow-up by next week.

Thanks,
Alicia Mendoza
Head of Product
Patchwork Labs

Attachments: patchwork_usage_q1-q2.csv (csv)

From: grace.oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Mendoza <alicia@patchworklabs.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-03T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Usage snapshot and renewal timing

Hi Alicia — thanks for this and the CSV, looks like a clear growth inflection (congrats on the product momentum). I ran a quick pass with Ben and Kimberly and a few pragmatic steps we can propose to finance/ops:

1) Short-term: burst credits + 6-week headroom
   - Offer: one-time 30% burst credit on your current committed rate for 8 weeks to absorb unpredictable peaks. (See attached offer PDF.)
   - Expected impact: smooths invoice variance and avoids throttling and retries that are inflating token counts.

2) Staged commit: a 3-month staged capacity commit
   - Phase A (weeks 0-6): 10% commit uplift with optional autoscaling threshold at 85% utilization.
   - Phase B (weeks 7-12): evaluate with actual traffic, if stable convert remaining uplift to a 12-month baseline.

3) Prefetch/prefix caching suggestions (low lift):
   - Enable prefix caching for repeated conversation starters (we see many near-identical user prompts). This typically reduces token spend on repeat prompts by ~15-25% on similar workloads.
   - For nightly batch jobs, adjust dedupe window: group similar inputs and reuse KV cache where possible instead of full re-encode.

4) Quick perf knobs to reduce retry overhead:
   - Increase request timeout in the batch pipeline by 20% while using larger batches (reduces retry storms).

I'll coordinate a short ROI summary with Ben (econ) and Kimberly (ops) and send a one-page for finance. Would you like that as a PDF or a short slide? Also suggest a 30-min call next Tuesday to walk finance through the numbers.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

On May 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT, Alicia Mendoza <alicia@patchworklabs.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Thanks again for the Q1 onboarding help — things are going well. We ran a quick internal audit...

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tactical renewal: usage audit + prefetching plan

Grace — drafting a concise ROI paragraph below and attaching a lightweight model profile that shows prefetch savings by endpoint. Key assumptions first:
- Baseline token unit cost (hosted) = $0.0009 per token equivalent (weighted mix).
- Current run rate (from CSV): ~2.1B tokens/month at peak week.
- Retry overhead & batch timeouts estimated to add ~9% incremental tokens.

ROI snapshot (6-week pilot with burst credits + prefetch):
- Direct savings from prefix caching: 16% of repeated prompt tokens -> ~336M tokens/month saved -> ~$302/month saved at baseline (note: numbers scale).
- Reduced retries from burst credits + timeout knob: removes the 9% overhead -> ~189M tokens/month avoided (~$170 saved).
- Net (conservative) first-month reduction: ~525M tokens -> ~$472 saved.

Non-dollar benefits:
- Fewer throttles = lower tail latency and fewer failed jobs, lower SRE toil.
- Predictability for finance during the staged commit window.

Attachments: prefetch_model_profile.json (json)

Ask: I can convert these into a single-slide ROI and an example invoice impact table. Grace, I recommend we offer: 8 weeks 30% burst credit + a 3-month staged commit (10% uplift) with an ops review at week 6. Kimberly/Tessa — can you confirm the operational feasibility of the dedupe window change and increasing the batch timeout?

—Ben
Senior Solutions Economist, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Mendoza <alicia@patchworklabs.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@patchworklabs.com
Date: 2025-05-06T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tactical renewal: usage audit + prefetching plan

Thanks Grace and Ben — this reads well and gives finance enough to start.

A couple of quick notes from our ops team (copied):
- We can accept a staged commit as long as the first 6 weeks are cancellable with 7-day notice.
- We'll try the dedupe window change in a canary lane this week and report back by Friday of next week.

Yes to the 30-min call next Tuesday (May 13) — please send a calendar invite. PDF is preferred for the exec summary and a single-slide ROI for the finance owner.

Alicia
Head of Product, Patchwork Labs
